entries.title: Show HN: I built a hardware processor that runs Python
entries.author: hwpythonner
entries.current_title: Show HN: I built a hardware processor that runs Python
entries.excerpt: Hi everyone, I built PyXL — a hardware processor that executes a custom assembly generated from Python programs, without using a traditional interpreter or virtual machine. It compiles Python -> CPython Bytecode -> Instruction set designed for direct hardware execution. I’m sharing an early benchmark: a GPIO test where PyXL achieves a 480ns round-trip toggle — compared to 14-25 micro seconds on a MicroPython Pyboard - even though PyXL runs at a lower clock (100MHz vs. 168MHz)
entries.guide_zh: PyXL 将 Python 编译到自定义指令集，交由专门硬件处理器执行。

entries.title: Show HN: Duolingo-style exercises but with real-world content like the news
entries.author: ph4evers
entries.current_title: Show HN: Duolingo-style exercises but with real-world content like the news
entries.excerpt: I've been working on a little side project that combines Duolingo-like listening comprehension exercises with real content . Every video is transcribed to get much better transcripts than the closed captions. I filter on high quality transcripts, and afterwards a LLM selects only plausible segments for the exercises. This seems to work well for quality control and seems to be reliable enough for these short exercises. Would love your thoughts!
entries.guide_zh: 用新闻等真实内容做多邻国式听力练习，先转录筛选再生成训练。
